concepts.def: Random Access Memory: volatile main memory holding running programs and data.
Read Only Memory: non-volatile memory holding firmware such as the bootloader.
Uses part of secondary storage as if it were RAM when main memory is full.
Hard Disk Drive: magnetic spinning-platter storage with high capacity but slower access than SSD.
Solid State Drive: flash-memory storage with no moving parts, faster than HDD.
Storage on CD, DVD or Blu-ray, read by a laser; useful for long-term distribution.
